en.html:
Kanae"In... out... In... out..."
Kageaki"It seems I have caused unnecessary mental strain. My apologies..."
Kanae"No... Though that was quite a shot straight to the heart."
Sayo"A splendid defeat, madam. In the human-shock competition, or whatever that was."
Kanae"Yes. Foul in the penalty area, I get a penalty kick, one goal practically guaranteed—and the third baseman does the hidden-ball trick. Runner out, game over. Judges total the scores, two to one, I lose by decision. That was the feeling."
Sayo"Next time you must enter straight through the wall, madam. According to quantum theory. At least that much effort is now required."
Kanae"Living in this world is becoming very difficult..."

en.html:
The clear answers stopped coming. A nice empty space opened up instead.
Kanae did not look like somebody caught in a careless remark. She was enjoying the pause. Taking her time with it.

Really, no answer was needed. She had already shown me where we stood.
Why no meeting with my tsurugi?
Because I must not be allowed to arm myself.
Why did my being armed concern her?
Because she and I were enemies.

Some conflict had arisen between the Prince and GHQ. When it did, she had acted for GHQ.
After everything she had said and done—and GHQ nearly wiping her out along with me on Enoshima—simple loyalty to her organisation probably did not explain it. But whatever the reason, here we were.
I owed the Prince. That put me on the other side.

Then why had she warned me about Kenchouji? A contradiction? Not necessarily. Perhaps she had wanted us gathered together, for one clean sweep.
It could all be explained. Only two things still refused to fit.
Why had GHQ and the Prince fallen out?
And why was I alive?
Kept alive. Put in a room in Yokohama, not killed.

Because she and I were enemies.

Some conflict had arisen between the Prince and GHQ. When it did, she had acted for GHQ.

ja.html:
明答続きの流れがここで途切れて、ぽっかりと間が
空いた。

　香奈枝嬢の表情は、失言を突かれて返答に詰まった
人間のそれではない。
　この間を楽しみ、味わっている、そんな顔だった。

　実際、返答の必要はない。
　彼女は既に明らかにしてみせたのだ。俺と彼女の、
立場関係を。

　劒冑との接触が許されないのは何故か。
　
　――武装させてはならないからだ。

　彼女がどうして俺の武装を危惧するのか。
　
　――彼女と俺とが敵対しているからだ。

　つまり。

　如何なる事情によってか、親王とＧＨＱの間に対立
が生じ。
　そしてその時、彼女はＧＨＱの立場で行動した。

　彼女のこれまでの言動、また江ノ島で俺もろともに
抹殺されかかっていた事を思えば、その理由は単純な
所属問題に帰すものでもないのだろうが……
　いずれにせよそうなった。

　必然、親王の恩を蒙る俺とも対立する。
　これと彼女が建朝寺襲撃を予報したこととは、矛盾
するようで必ずしもそうでない。まとめて一掃する為
にそうしただけなのかもしれないからだ。

　全て説明がつく。
　あとわからないのは……親王とＧＨＱの対立の理由
と。

　もう一つ。
　<ruby>なぜ俺がいま生きているのか<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　生かされているのか。
　殺されず、横浜に拘禁されているのか。

en.html:
Four o'clock chimed. Only then did I notice the clock. Quite a fine wall clock, in fact. Far too fine for this little Western-style prison cell.

What had the person installing it been thinking? No windows, no way to tell day from night, so at least give the poor fellow a decent clock?
Or put one good thing here to make the rest look even more miserable?
Perhaps malicious kindness. Exact time remaining before execution, so the prisoner could prepare himself properly.
Or perhaps they had one spare clock. Bas. All my analysis, and it could simply be a spare clock.

際立たせて収容者を追い詰める謀略か。

決めさせようという悪意<ruby>滴<rt>したた</rt></ruby>る親切か。
